title: One question per candidate
statement: With many candidates, ask one yes-or-no question about each and combine the answers in code.
example: A twelve-way choice returned nothing at all.
detail:
When a judgment has many candidates, the reading engine asks one bounded question per candidate and composes the
answers in code; a wide choice is where it kept failing, three times over
(`grade3-reading/engine/EVIDENCE-2026-09-22.md`). A twelve-way choice spread its probability and returned nothing at
all (`grade3-reading/engine/src/goal/from-text.js`). Where a choice remains, it carries a none-of-these option, since
silence beats a line that doesn't fit (`grade3-reading/engine/src/goal/hunt.js`).

A model asked for an overall grade drifts generous; a model asked one concrete thing stays honest.

Never use a single wide choice. Probability spreads across similar options and clears no support gate, so you get nothing back. This failure cost a lesson binding, every taught word, and most illustrations before it was fixed.
